title: Temurah 2
description: The first daf of Temurah: everyone, men and women, can substitute a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one, though it is forbidden and earns forty lashes; whether an heir, a minor or a gentile can do so too, and Rami bar Ḥama’s dilemma about a gentile’s offering that atones for a Jew.
topics: 🔄 “This in place of that”: substitution is forbidden, yet it takes effect
⚖️ Ab initio or after the fact? Rav Yehuda rereads the mishna
👨‍👦 The heir: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda on placing hands and substitution
✋ Three times “his offering”: a gentile’s, another’s, a father’s, and joint owners
👩 “And if he shall at all substitute”: including a woman, though the Torah already equates her punishments
🧒 Rami bar Ḥama’s dilemmas: a minor at the age of vows, and a gentile
🏛️ The consecrated animals of gentiles: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yosei
🐑 The one who consecrates and the one who achieves atonement

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל מְמִירִין, אֶחָד אֲנָשִׁים וְאֶחָד נָשִׁים. לֹא שֶׁאָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהָמִיר, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הֵמִיר — מוּמָר, וְסוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים.

a2.he: גְּמָ׳ הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא: אָמְרַתְּ ״הַכֹּל מְמִירִין״ — לְכַתְּחִילָּה, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי ״לֹא שֶׁאָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהָמִיר אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הֵמִיר מוּמָר״ — דִּיעֲבַד!

a3.he: וְתִיסְבְּרָא ״הַכֹּל מְמִירִין״ — לְכַתְּחִילָּה? אַדְּקַשְׁיָא לָךְ מִמַּתְנִיתִין, תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ קְרָא! דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ״.

a4.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָכִי קָתָנֵי — הַכֹּל מַתְפִּיסִין בִּתְמוּרָה, אֶחָד אֲנָשִׁים וְאֶחָד נָשִׁים, לֹא שֶׁאָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהָמִיר, שֶׁאִם הֵמִיר — מוּמָר, וְסוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים.

a5.he: הַכׇּל לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי יוֹרֵשׁ, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a6.he: דִּתְנַן: יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ, יוֹרֵשׁ מֵמִיר — דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ, וְיוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵמִיר.

a7.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? — יָלֵיף תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ מִסּוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ: מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ, אַף תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ — יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵמִיר.

a8.he: וּסְמִיכָה גּוּפַהּ מְנָלַן? תְּלָת ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ כְּתִיבִי: חַד — ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן גּוֹי, וְחַד — ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן חֲבֵירוֹ, וְחַד — ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ וְלֹא קׇרְבַּן אָבִיו.

a9.he: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ, וְהָכְתִיב ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״! הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה.

a10.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה לֵית לֵיהּ. מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּהָא לָא מְיַחַד קׇרְבָּן דִּידְהוּ. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם אִית לֵיהּ, וְקׇרְבַּן גּוֹי וְקׇרְבַּן חֲבֵירוֹ מֵחַד קְרָא נָפְקָא, דְּאִיַּיתַּר לֵיהּ חַד לְבַעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה.

a11.he: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר יוֹרֵשׁ מֵמִיר, מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר לָךְ: ״אִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״ לְרַבּוֹת הַיּוֹרֵשׁ,

b1.he: וְיָלֵיף סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ מִתְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ, מָה תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ מֵימִר, אַף סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹרֵשׁ סוֹמֵךְ.

b2.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה. וְכִדְתַנְיָא: לְפִי שֶׁכׇּל הָעִנְיָן כּוּלּוֹ אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן זָכָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ״, אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה.

b3.he: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אִשָּׁה מְנָא לֵיהּ? נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וְּאִם״. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, ״וְאִם״ לָא דָּרֵישׁ.

b4.he: וּבֵין רַבִּי מֵאִיר וּבֵין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי קְרָא לְאִשָּׁה, הָא לָא רַבְּיַיהּ קְרָא — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כִּי עָבְדָא תְּמוּרָה לָא לָקְיָא. וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַעֲשׂוּ מִכׇּל חַטֹּאת הָאָדָם״ — הִשְׁוָה הַכָּתוּב אִשָּׁה לְאִישׁ לְכׇל עֳונָשִׁין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה!

b5.he: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי עוֹנֶשׁ דְּשָׁוֶה בֵּין בְּיָחִיד בֵּין בְּצִבּוּר, אֲבָל הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעוֹנֶשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל הוּא, דִּתְנַן: אֵין הַצִּבּוּר וְהַשּׁוּתָּפִין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה — אִשָּׁה נָמֵי כִּי עָבְדָא לָא לָקְיָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b6.he: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: קָטָן מַהוּ שֶׁיָּמִיר? הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּקָטָן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים — לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּכֵיוָן אַקְדּוֹשֵׁי לָא אַקְדֵּישׁ, אֲמוֹרֵי מֵמַיר? אֶלָּא כִּי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ — בְּקָטָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים.

b7.he: מִי אָמְרִינַן, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: ״אִישׁ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״כִּי יַפְלִיא נֶדֶר״ — לְרַבּוֹת מוּפְלָא הַסָּמוּךְ לְאִישׁ, דְּקׇדְשׁוֹ קָדוֹשׁ. מִדְּאַקְדּוֹשֵׁי מַקְדֵּישׁ, אֲמוֹרֵי נָמֵי מֵמַיר, אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בַּר עוּנְשִׁין הוּא, בִּתְמוּרָה לָא מִיתְּפִיס?

b8.he: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר קָטָן עָבֵיד תְּמוּרָה, דְּהָא אָתֵי לִכְלַל עֳונָשִׁין, גּוֹי מַהוּ שֶׁיָּמִיר? מִי אָמְרַתְּ מִדְּאַקְדּוֹשֵׁי מַקְדֵּישׁ, דְּתַנְיָא: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״? לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַגּוֹיִם, שֶׁנּוֹדְרִים נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲמוֹרֵי נָמֵי מֵמַיר. אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אָתֵי לִכְלַל עֳונָשִׁין, כִּי עָבֵיד תְּמוּרָה לָא קָדְשָׁה?

b9.he: אָמַר רָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: קׇדְשֵׁי גוֹיִם — לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין, וְאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל, נוֹתָר וְטָמֵא, אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין מְבִיאִין עֲלֵיהֶם נְסָכִים, אֲבָל קׇרְבָּנוֹ טָעוּן נְסָכִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

b10.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּכוּלָּן אֲנִי רוֹאֶה לְהַחְמִיר. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, אֲבָל בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן. קָתָנֵי מִיהָא: אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה!

b11.he: וְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, בְּהִקְדִּישׁ גּוֹי לְהִתְכַּפֵּר גּוֹי — לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי — בְּהִקְדִּישׁ גּוֹי וּמִתְכַּפֵּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: בָּתַר מַקְדִּישׁ אָזְלִינַן, אוֹ בָּתַר מִתְכַּפֵּר אָזְלִינַן?

b12.he: תִּיפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ, וּמִתְכַּפֵּר עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְהַתּוֹרֵם מִשֶּׁלּוֹ

messages.text: 2a
Masechet Temurah begins · מסכת תמורה
Chapter 1 · הכל ממירין · HaKol Memirin: who can substitute a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one, and what follows when they do.
Mishna
Everyone substitutes a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal, both men and women.

notes.he: בהמת חולין זו תחת זו של הקדש:
notes.en: Everyone substitutes: [saying of] a non-sacred animal, “This one is in place of that one” of consecrated property.

notes.dh: מתני' הכל ממירין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים
notes.he: בהכל שוחטין לא תני אחד אנשים ואחד נשים ובגמ' מפרש משום דכל הפרשה כולה בלשון זכר נאמרה איצטריך קרא לרבויי נשים:
notes.en: Everyone substitutes, both men and women: In [the mishna] “Everyone slaughters” [Ḥullin 2a] it does not teach “both men and women.” And the Gemara [here, 2b] explains why: since the whole passage is stated in the masculine, a verse was needed to include women.

messages.text: That is not to say that it is permitted for a person to effect substitution; rather, it means that if one substituted a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal, the substitution takes effect, and the non-sacred animal becomes consecrated, and the consecrated animal remains sacred.

notes.he: דהא כתיב לא ימיר:
notes.en: Not that a person is permitted to substitute: since it is written: “He shall not … substitute.”

notes.he: דמתפיס עלה קדושה ושתיהן קדושות:
notes.en: It is substituted: for he applies sanctity to it, and both of them are sacred.

messages.text: And the one who substituted the non-sacred animal incurs the forty [sofeg et ha’arba’im] lashes.

notes.he: משום לאו דלא ימיר:
notes.en: And he incurs the forty: on account of the prohibition “He shall not substitute.”

notes.he: וא"ת אמאי לא תני שמונים דהא כתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳) לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו ויש לומר דלא נחת למנין מלקיות אלא כלומר דלקי עליה ועוד י"ל דלעולם לא לקי אלא ארבעים ותרי לאוי צריכי חד בקרבן שלו וחד בשל חבירו וכגון דאמר כל הרוצה להמיר יבא וימיר:
notes.en: And he incurs the forty: And if you say: why does it not teach eighty, since it is written (Leviticus 27:10): “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it” [two prohibitions]? One can say that it does not come to give the number of lashes, but means only that he is flogged for it. And one can further say that in fact he is flogged only forty, and the two prohibitions are both needed: one for his own offering and one for another’s, for example where [the owner] said: Whoever wishes to substitute, let him come and substitute.

messages.caption: Substitution in brief: saying “This is in place of that” makes both animals sacred; it is forbidden, yet it takes effect, and the one who does it is flogged. Below, who can effect substitution, as this daf discusses it.

messages.text: Gemara
This mishna itself is difficult: You say that everyone substitutes a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one, which indicates that substitution may be performed ab initio.
messages.lead: The Gemara notes an apparent contradiction in the mishna:

messages.text: And then you teach: That is not to say that it is permitted for a person to effect substitution; rather, it means only that if one unlawfully substituted a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal, the substitution takes effect, indicating that it is effective only after the fact.

notes.he: בתמיה. דלכתחלה אינו רשאי להמיר אבל דיעבד שפיר דמי:
notes.en: Not that a person is permitted … after the fact: [this is said] in astonishment. [The clause implies] that ab initio one is not permitted to substitute, but after the fact it is fine.

notes.dh: הא גופא קשיא אמרת הכל ממירין לכתחלה לא שאדם רשאי להמיר דיעבד
notes.he: וא"ת מנא ליה למקשה דהכל ממירין לכתחלה הוא דלמא דיעבד הוא דכה"ג פריך בריש חולין (דף ב.) וצ"ל דע"כ הכל ממירין לכתחלה דאי דיעבד תרתי דיעבד למה לי וכן (פרש"י) [איתא] התם דר"ל דהכל שוחטין לכתחילה דאי דיעבד תרתי דיעבד למה לי ופירש רבינו שלמה זכרונו לברכה התם דלכך לא קשה הכא תרתי דיעבד למה לי משום דאשמועינן בסיפא שסופג ארבעים דסד"א לאו שאין בו מעשה הוא ואין לוקין עליו ולפירושו קשה מאי פריך הכא ואין לומר דהיינו האי דקמשני דאין הלשון משמע כן ועוד מאי קמשני ממה שהקשה ופר"ת דתנן הכל ממירין דלישנא אלימא לאשמועינן דאפילו במזיד התמורה נתפסת וסד"א ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר והיינו הא דקא משני וא"ת והיכי מצי למימר דתנא לישנא אלימא משום חידוש דמזיד הא אמר לקמן יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד אלמא משמע דמזיד פשיטא טפי משוגג ותירץ רבינו ברוך דהא דאמר יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד לענין מלקות קאמר ורבינו שמשון משנ"ץ חלק עליו דהא אמרי' אין מלקות בשוגג ויש ספרים חלוקין בדבר לקמן (תמורה דף יז.) דקאמר גבי תמורה לקי גבי קדשים לא לקי ואית דגרסי גבי תמורה קדוש גבי קדשים לא קדוש וי"א דהא דאמר יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד היינו לענין מתפס קדושה דאמר בעלמא הקדש בטעות לא הוי הקדש ומש"ה פשיט טפי במזיד מבשוגג והא דאמר הכא דתנא הכל ממירין משום רבותא דמזיד היינו לענין הקרבה דאמר לקמן התמורה נמי קריבה ואשמעינן הכא דאף במזיד קריבה דס"ד ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר וכל זה לא נהירא לר"י מדקמשני רב יהודה הכי קתני הכל מתפיסין בתמורה אחד אנשים ואחד נשים ומה לו להזכיר אחד אנשים ואחד נשים לכן פר"י דתנא בהכל ממירין לישנא אלימא משום נשים דאמר לקמן דכל הענין מדבר בלשון זכר וכתיב המר ימיר לרבויי נשים דסד"א אהני מיעוטא ואהני ריבויא אהני ריבויא לאשמועינן דתמורת נשים קדשי ואהני מיעוטא דלא מקרבן לכך תנא הכל ממירין לישנא אלימא דקריבה כמו תמורת אנשים:
notes.en: In brief: How does the questioner know that “Everyone substitutes” means ab initio, when it might mean after the fact, as the parallel question at the beginning of Ḥullin (2a) asks? It must mean ab initio, for otherwise why would the mishna say “after the fact” twice; Reish Lakish argues the same about “Everyone slaughters” there. Rashi explained in Ḥullin that “twice after the fact” is no difficulty here, because the latter clause adds that he incurs forty lashes, though one might have thought a prohibition without an action carries no lashes. But on his explanation, what is the Gemara asking here? One cannot say that this is its answer, since the wording does not imply it, and then the answer would add nothing to the question. Rabbeinu Tam explains that the mishna uses strong language, “Everyone substitutes,” to teach that the substitution takes hold even when done intentionally, lest one say: forty lashes on his shoulders, and [the original stays] valid; and that is the Gemara’s answer. But below it says “it shall be” includes the unintentional like the intentional, implying that the intentional case is the more obvious. Rabbeinu Barukh answers that that teaching is about lashes; Rabbeinu Shimshon of Sens disagrees, since there are no lashes for an unintentional act. The texts differ on this below (17a): some read “with substitution he is flogged, with consecrated animals he is not flogged,” and some read “with substitution it is sacred, with consecrated animals it is not sacred.” Others say “it shall be” refers to the sanctity taking hold, since consecration in error is generally not consecration, so the intentional case is the more obvious; and the novelty of the intentional case here concerns sacrifice, since it says below that the substitute too is sacrificed, and the mishna teaches that it is sacrificed even when substituted intentionally. None of this seems right to the Ri, since Rav Yehuda’s answer, “Everyone can apply by substitution, both men and women,” would have no reason to mention men and women. So the Ri explains that the mishna uses the strong language “Everyone substitutes” because of women: the whole passage is in the masculine, and “hamer yamir” comes to include women, so one might have thought that both the exclusion and the inclusion take effect, the inclusion making a woman’s substitute sacred and the exclusion keeping it from being sacrificed. Therefore the mishna says “Everyone substitutes”: a woman’s substitute is sacrificed like a man’s. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: And can you understand the phrase: Everyone substitutes, as indicating that substitution may be performed ab initio? If so, before the mishna poses a difficulty for you, the verse should pose a difficulty for you, as it is written: “He shall not alter it, nor substitute it” (Leviticus 27:10). The verse clearly states that it is prohibited to perform substitution.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: ומתני' קתני דהכל ממירין אפי' לכתחלה:
notes.en: Nor substitute it: and yet the mishna teaches that everyone substitutes, even ab initio.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is teaching: Everyone can apply the status of a consecrated animal to a non-sacred animal by the act of substitution, both men and women.

notes.dh: ה"ג אלא הכי קתני הכל מתפיסין בתמורה אחד כו'
notes.he: כלומר שתופסת קדושת תמורה בבהמה בין על פי אנשים בין על פי נשים ומשמע (אפי') דיעבד כמו דאם המירה אפילו אשה תופסת על פיה קדושת תמורה ולא שאדם רשאי להמיר כו':
notes.en: This is the reading: “Rather, this is what it is teaching: Everyone can apply [sanctity] by substitution, both men…,” etc. That is, the sanctity of substitution takes hold of an animal whether by the word of men or by the word of women. And this implies after the fact: that if she substituted, the sanctity of substitution takes hold even by a woman’s word; “but not that a person is permitted to substitute,” etc.

notes.dh: אמר רב יהודה הכי קתני מתניתין הכל ממירין מתפיסין בתמורה
notes.he: הכל שאמרו תהא זו תחת זו נתפס זה תחת זה וזהו פירוש הכל ממירין ולא משמע דממירין לכתחילה ואהכי קתני ולא שאדם רשאי להמיר [כלומר אע"ג דהכל מתפיסין לא שאדם רשאי להמיר] לכתחילה:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda said: This is what our mishna teaches: “Everyone substitutes” [means] they apply [sanctity] by substitution: everyone who said, “Let this be in place of that,” this one takes hold in place of that one. That is the meaning of “Everyone substitutes,” and it does not imply that they substitute ab initio. And therefore it teaches: “Not that a person is permitted to substitute” [that is, although everyone applies sanctity, it is not that a person is permitted to substitute] ab initio.

messages.text: But that is not to say that it is permitted for a person to effect substitution, as, if one did effect substitution, the substitution takes effect only after the fact, and he incurs the forty lashes.
What does the comprehensive term: Everyone, serve to include?

notes.he: הכל לאיתויי כלומר מאי שייר דלא תנא:
notes.en: “Everyone,” to include: that is, what did it leave out, that it did not teach?

messages.text: It serves to include an inheritor, and accordingly, this mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: שהמיר בקרבן שהפריש אביו בחייו שתמורתו תמורה:
notes.en: An inheritor: who substituted for an offering his father had set aside in his lifetime; his substitute is a substitute.

notes.he: [לאיתויי יורש דמימר:
notes.en: To include an inheritor, who substitutes.

messages.text: An inheritor who inherited a consecrated animal places his hands on the head of the offering when he sacrifices it as would the original owner, and likewise an inheritor is able to substitute a non-sacred animal for the consecrated one that he inherited. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: על קרבן אביו שהפרישו אביו בחייו ולא הספיק להקריבו עד שמת:
notes.en: An inheritor places hands: on his father’s offering, which his father set aside in his lifetime and did not manage to sacrifice before he died.

messages.text: An inheritor does not place his hands on the head of the offering when he sacrifices it, and an inheritor does not substitute a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one that he inherited. These acts may be performed only by the one who initially consecrated the animal.
The mishna indicates that an inheritor is able to effect substitution, contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.
What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda?

notes.he: דאמר יורש אינו ממיר:
notes.en: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda: who said that an inheritor does not substitute.

messages.text: He derives the halakhot of the animal’s initial consecration from the end of the consecration, i.e., the sacrifice of the consecrated animal, as follows: Just as with regard to the end of a consecrated animal, an inheritor does not place his hands on the head of the offering before slaughter, so too, with regard to the initial consecration, an inheritor does not effect substitution to consecrate the animal.

notes.dh: ה"ג יליף תחילת הקדש מסוף הקדש
notes.he: גמר התחלת הקדש כגון תמורה:
notes.en: This is the reading: “He derives the initial consecration from the end of consecration”: he derives the beginning of consecration, such as substitution,

notes.he: דהיינו סמיכה דהויא סמוך לשחיטה. ואי קשיא והא קרי לה לתמורה סוף הקדש במסכת נזיר (דף לא.) משום דלא איירי התם בסמיכה כלל והויא לה תמורה סוף הקדש לגבי קרבן שהמירו בו דאותו קרבן הוי ראשון וחילופיו הוי שני אבל הכא דקא משתעינן בסמיכה הויא לה תמורה תחילת הקדש לגבי סמיכה שהיא לבסוף תיכף לשחיטה:
notes.en: from the end of consecration: that is, placing hands, which is close to the slaughter. And if you find it difficult that in Tractate Nazir (31a) substitution is called the end of consecration: that is because there it does not discuss placing hands at all, so substitution is the end of consecration relative to the offering for which it was substituted, since that offering is first and its exchange is second. But here, where we are speaking of placing hands, substitution is the beginning of consecration relative to placing hands, which comes at the end, immediately before the slaughter.

notes.he: כמו תמורה מסוף הקדש דהיינו סמיכה דהוא סמוך לשחיטה ולהכי קרי לתמורה סוף הקדש (כמו) במסכת נזיר (דף לא.) משום דלא אמרינן התם בסמיכה כלל והוה ליה תמורה סוף הקדש לגבי קרבן שהמירו בו דאותו קרבן הוי ראשון וחילופיו שני אבל הכא דקמשתעינן בסמיכה הוה ליה תמורה תחילת הקדש לגבי סמיכה שהיא לבסוף תיכף לשחיטה. לשון רש"י:
notes.en: The initial consecration: such as substitution; from the end of consecration: that is, placing hands, which is close to the slaughter. And the reason substitution is called the end of consecration in Tractate Nazir (31a) is that there we do not speak of placing hands at all, so substitution is the end of consecration relative to the offering for which it was substituted, since that offering is first and its exchange second. But here, where we speak of placing hands, substitution is the beginning of consecration relative to placing hands, which comes at the end, immediately before the slaughter. [This is] Rashi’s wording.

notes.he: מקיש ר' יהודה תחלת הקדש דהיינו תמורה שעכשו מכניסה להא תמורה תחילה בהקדש לסוף הקדש דהיינו סמיכה דתיכף לה שחיטה דהיינו סוף הקדש דכשהוא שוחטה מיכליא הקדש ומה סוף הקדש יורש אינו סומך דכתיב על ראש קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו הכי נמי אין מימר ואמר לי ר' דאף במסכ' נזיר [דף לא.] משמע תחילת הקדש הזבח עצמו וסוף הקדש משמע תמורתו. והיינו טעמא דהתם לא מיירי בסמיכה והכא מיירי בסמיכה משמע כדאמרן. ואלא רבנן דסברי דיורש סומך הא כת' קרבנו דמשמע למעוטי כלומר קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו סברי רבנן תלתא קרבנו כתיבי בסמיכה גבי שלמים ולא קרבן אביו סברי רבנן עובד כוכבים דאין קרבן עובד כוכבים טעון סמיכה ולא קרבן חבירו דאין אדם סומך על קרבן חבירו]:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda juxtaposes the beginning of consecration, that is, substitution, which one now brings into consecration, so that substitution is a beginning in consecration, with the end of consecration, that is, placing hands, which is immediately followed by slaughter; that is the end of consecration, for when he slaughters it the consecration is complete. Just as at the end of consecration an inheritor does not place hands, as it is written “on the head of his offering,” and not his father’s offering, so too he does not substitute. And my teacher told me that in Tractate Nazir (31a) as well, the beginning of consecration means the offering itself and the end of consecration means its substitute; the reason is that there it does not discuss placing hands, while here it does, so the meaning is as we said. And as for the Rabbis [that is, Rabbi Meir’s view], who hold that an inheritor places hands: isn’t “his offering” written, which implies an exclusion, that is, his offering and not his father’s offering? The Rabbis hold: three [times] “his offering” are written about placing hands with the peace offering: [one excludes] a gentile [the printed text here also reads “and not his father’s offering,” which seems out of place], since a gentile’s offering does not require placing hands; and [one,] not another’s offering, since a person does not place hands on another’s offering.

messages.text: And from where do we derive the halakha of placing hands itself?

notes.he: דיורש אינו סומך:
notes.en: From where do we [derive it]: that an inheritor does not place hands.

messages.text: The term “his offering” is written three times in the passage discussing a peace offering, in connection with the placing of hands (Leviticus 3:2, 8, 12). One instance teaches that the requirement of placing hands applies to his offering but not the offering of a gentile. And one instance teaches that it applies to his offering but not the offering of another, as only the owner places his hands on the offering. And one instance teaches that it applies to his offering but not the offering of his father, as an inheritor does not place his hands on an offering he inherited.

verse.he: וְסָמַךְ יָדוֹ עַל־רֹאשׁ קׇרְבָּנוֹ וּשְׁחָטוֹ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְזָרְקוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים אֶת־הַדָּם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב׃
verse.en: You shall lay a hand upon the head of your offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting; and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall dash the blood against all sides of the altar.

notes.he: בשלמים בפ' ויקרא מואם זבח שלמים קרבנו עד ואם עז קרבנו ובשלשתם כתיב סמיכה:
notes.en: “His offering” is written three times: with the peace offering, in Parashat Vayikra, from “And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings” until “And if his offering be a goat,” and in all three placing hands is written.

notes.he: וא"ת למאי איצטריך קרבנו להכי הא נפקא שפיר מבני ישראל סומכין ואין העובדי כוכבים סומכין ויש לומר דאיצטריך דמהו דתימא אין העובד כוכבים עצמו סומך על קרבנו ומיהו הכהנים סומכין עליהן ומש"ה איצטריך קרבנו לומר שאין בקרבן עובד כוכבים סמיכה כלל:
notes.en: His offering, and not the offering of a gentile: And if you say: why is “his offering” needed for this? It is already derived from “the children of Israel … and he shall place”: the children of Israel place hands, and gentiles do not. One can say that it is needed, lest you say that the gentile himself does not place hands on his offering, but the priests place hands on it instead; therefore “his offering” is needed, to say that a gentile’s offering has no placing of hands at all.

messages.text: But according to Rabbi Meir, who said that an inheritor places his hands on the head of the offering when he sacrifices it, isn’t the term “his offering” written in the verse? How does he interpret the third instance of that term?

notes.he: דמשמע על קרבן עצמו הוא סומך ולא על קרבן אביו:
notes.en: Isn’t “his offering” written: which implies that he places hands on his own offering, and not on his father’s offering.

messages.text: He requires that term to include all joint owners [ba’alei ḥoverin] in the halakha of placing hands, to teach that they all must place their hands on the offering’s head.

notes.he: שאם נשתתפו ב' או ג' על קרבן אחד קרינא אכל חד וחד קרבנו וכולן סומכין בו:
notes.en: Joint owners in placing hands: that if two or three became partners in one offering, we call it “his offering” for each and every one of them, and all of them place hands on it.

notes.he: שאם הקריבו שנים או שלשה קרבן אחד כולן סומכין עליו דלכל חד קרינן ליה קרבנו וסבירא ליה דיורש סומך דקרבן אביו דמי כמו קרבנו של יורש:
notes.en: All joint owners in placing hands: that if two or three brought one offering, all of them place hands on it, since for each one we call it “his offering.” And he holds that an inheritor places hands, since his father’s offering is like the inheritor’s own offering.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yehuda, he does not accept that joint owners are included in the requirement of placing hands. What is the reason for this? The reason is that their offering is not specific to one person and is therefore not included in the term “his offering.”

notes.he: דודאי אינו טעון סמיכה כיון דלא מייחד קרבן דידהו כלומר כיון דלא הוי חלוט אכל אחד ואחד וכי כתיב קרא לקרבנו ולא לקרבן אביו:
notes.en: He does not accept it: certainly it does not require placing hands [by each owner], since their offering is not specific; that is, since it does not wholly belong to each one. And when the verse is written, it is for “his offering, and not his father’s offering.”

notes.dh: ור' יהודה כל בעלי חוברין לסמיכה לית ליה
notes.he: אייתר ליה חד קרבנו למעוטי יורש:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda does not accept all joint owners in placing hands: so one “his offering” remains for him to exclude the inheritor.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead that actually, he accepts that one instance of “his offering” serves to include joint owners, and he derives both the halakha of the offering of a gentile and that of the offering of another from one verse, so that one instance of the term “his offering” remains for him to include joint owners in the requirement of placing hands on the head of an offering, and the third instance serves to teach that an inheritor does not place hands on the offering of his father.

notes.he: דמשמע קרבנו ולא שליח בין של ישראל בין של עובד כוכבים דלמעוטי עובד כוכבים עצמו שלא יסמוך לא צריך דאמרינן במנחות (דף צג.) ובתורת כהנים בני ישראל וסמך בני ישראל סומכין ואין העובדי כוכבים סומכין:
notes.en: Derived from one verse: which implies: his offering, and not [one who acts] as an agent [on another’s offering], whether of a Jew or of a gentile. For to exclude the gentile himself from placing hands no verse is needed, as we say in Menaḥot (93a) and in Torat Kohanim: “The children of Israel … and he shall place”: the children of Israel place hands, and gentiles do not place hands.

notes.he: ואכתי הוי קרבנו שלישי לקרבנו ולא קרבן אביו [דס"ד] דשל אביו לאו כלאחר דמי אלא כשלו:
notes.en: And one remains for him, etc.: and there still remains the third “his offering”: his offering, and not his father’s offering, [for it might have entered your mind] that his father’s offering is not like another’s but like his own.

notes.he: לרבויי כל בעלי חוברין ומהיכא יליף ליה הא קא משוי חד קרבנו למעוטי יורש וחד למעוטי קרבן עובד כוכבים וחד למעוטי קרבן חבירו. לא ר' יהודה קרבן חבירו וקרבן עובד כוכבים מחד קרא נפקא ליה דתרוייהו אינן שלו אייתר ליה חד לרבויי כל בעלי חוברין:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: in fact he accepts that it includes all joint owners. And from where does he derive it? Doesn’t he use one “his offering” to exclude the inheritor, one to exclude a gentile’s offering and one to exclude another’s offering? No: Rabbi Yehuda derives another’s offering and a gentile’s offering from one verse, since neither of them is his own; one remains for him to include all joint owners.

messages.caption: How each view spends the three mentions of “his offering”, and where the heir stands. Rabbi Meir’s first two uses follow Rabbeinu Gershom.

messages.text: And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, who said that an inheritor can effect substitution?

notes.dh: ורבי מאיר דאמר יורש מימר מאי טעמא
notes.he: ואם תאמר אמאי איצטריך טעמא לר' מאיר כיון דלית ליה קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו אלמא אית ליה יורש סומך ואם כן אית ליה למימר דהא ילפינן זה מזה ויש לומר דאי לאו קרא דהמר ימיר דמרבה יורש הוה ליה לאוקומיה קרבנו טפי למעוטי יורש מלרבות כל בעלי חוברין אבל השתא דכתיב ואם המר ימיר לרבות יורש דסומך ומוקי קרבנו לרבות כל בעלי חוברין וא"ת מאי שנא דשאר קרבנו למעוטי והאי לרבויי ויש לומר דלמעוטי לא מצית אמרת דאם כן לישתוק קרא מיניה וממילא אמר דאין השותפין סומכין כדאמר לקמן (תמורה דף יג.) דאין השותפין ממירין:
notes.en: And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, who said an inheritor substitutes: And if you say: why is a reason needed for Rabbi Meir? Since he does not expound “his offering, and not his father’s offering,” he evidently holds that an inheritor places hands, and if so he should derive substitution from it, since we derive one from the other. One can say: were it not for the verse “hamer yamir,” which includes the inheritor, he would have had to interpret “his offering” as excluding the inheritor rather than as including all joint owners. But now that “And if he shall at all substitute” is written to include the inheritor, who [therefore] places hands, he interprets “his offering” as including all joint owners. And if you say: why are the other mentions of “his offering” exclusions and this one an inclusion? One can say that you cannot read it as an exclusion, for then the verse could have been silent, and it would follow by itself that partners do not place hands, just as it says below (13a) that partners do not substitute.

messages.text: Rabbi Meir could say to you that the repetition of the verb in the verse: “And if he shall at all substitute [hamer yamir] animal for animal” (Leviticus 27:10), serves to include the inheritor,

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: דהכי מצי למיכתב ואם ימיר בהמה בבהמה המר ימיר למאי הלכתא לרבות את היורש דתמורתו תמורה:
notes.en: To include the inheritor: since it could have written: “And if he shall substitute animal for animal” [with the verb once]. “Hamer yamir”: for what halakha? To include the inheritor, that his substitute is a substitute.

messages.text: 2b

and he derives the halakhot of the end of a consecrated animal from the initial consecration of the animal, as follows: Just as with regard to the initial state of consecration of the animal, an inheritor can effect substitution, so too, with regard to the end of the consecrated animal, an inheritor places his hands on its head.

notes.he: הכי גרסינן ויליף סוף הקדש מתחלת הקדש כו':
notes.en: This is the reading: “And he derives the end of consecration from the initial consecration,” etc.

messages.text: According to Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that an inheritor is not able to effect substitution, what does he do with this repetitive language in the verse: “And if he shall at all substitute”? How does he interpret it?
It serves to include a woman as able to effect substitution and to incur the penalty of forty lashes for doing so.

notes.he: שתמורתה תמורה ולקיא משום לאו דלא ימיר:
notes.en: The woman: that her substitute is a substitute, and she is flogged on account of the prohibition “He shall not substitute.”

messages.text: Since the verses concerning the entire matter of substitution speak only in the masculine, as it is stated: “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it” (Leviticus 27:10), from where is it derived that a woman is included? The verse states: “And if he shall at all substitute,” to include a woman.
messages.lead: And this is as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.dh: אלא בלשון זכר דכתיב לא יחליפנו
notes.he: דהיינו לשון זכר ולא כתיב לא תחליפנו דהוי לשון נקבה:
notes.en: Only in the masculine, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it [lo yaḥalifenu]”: which is the masculine form; it is not written lo taḥalifenu, which would be the feminine form.

notes.he: כלומר מהיכן נלמוד שסופנו לרבות את האשה:
notes.en: What will we ultimately include, etc.: that is, from where will we learn that we are ultimately to include the woman? [Rashi’s text of the baraita reads “What will we ultimately include” where the printed text, and the Davidson English, have “from where is a woman derived.”]

notes.he: מדכתיב קרא תרי זימני:
notes.en: The verse states: “And if he shall at all substitute”: since the verse writes [the verb] twice.

notes.he: כלומר מהכא נלמד שסופינו לרבות את האשה שעושה תמורה ת"ל המר ימיר ריבה. [ורבנן נפקא להון אשה מואם המר מוי"ו דמאם דמיותר דלא צריך למיכתבי:
notes.en: What will we ultimately include? The woman. That is, from here we learn that we are ultimately to include the woman, that she effects substitution: the verse states “hamer yamir,” it included [her]. [And the Rabbis derive the woman from “and if”: from the vav of “and if,” which is superfluous and need not have been written.] [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text, like Rashi’s, reads “What will we ultimately include”; by “the Rabbis” he means the view the Gemara gives as Rabbi Meir’s.]

messages.text: And according to Rabbi Meir, who derives a different halakha from that verse, from where does he derive that a woman is included?

notes.he: דאיצטריך ליה ואם המר ימיר לרבות יורש אשה מנא ליה:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Meir: who needs “And if he shall at all substitute” to include the inheritor: from where does he derive a woman?

messages.text: He derives it from the addition of the conjunction “and” in the verse: “And if he shall at all substitute.” And Rabbi Yehuda does not interpret the term “and if” as having any special significance.

notes.he: מדמצי למכתב אם המר ימיר וכתיב ואם:
notes.en: He derives it from the vav: since it could have written “If he shall at all substitute,” and it writes “And if.”

messages.text: And according to both the opinion of Rabbi Meir and the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, the reason why a woman is included is that the verse explicitly includes a woman, either by adding a conjunction or by repetition of the verb. Should one infer that if the verse did not include a woman, I would say that when a woman performs an act of substitution she is not flogged?

notes.he: דאם המירה תמורתה אינה תמורה:
notes.en: She is not flogged: [that is,] if she substituted, her substitute is not a substitute.

messages.text: When the verse states: “When a man or woman shall commit any sin that people commit” (Numbers 5:6), the verse equates a woman with a man with regard to all punishments of the Torah.
messages.lead: But didn’t Rav Yehuda say that Rav says, and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ אוֹ־אִשָּׁה כִּי יַעֲשׂוּ מִכׇּל־חַטֹּאת הָאָדָם לִמְעֹל מַעַל בַּיהֹוָה וְאָשְׁמָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelites: When a man or woman has committed any wrong toward a fellow human being, thus breaking faith with GOD, and they have realized their guilt,

messages.text: Why, then, is there a need for the verse to include women in the prohibition against substitution?

It was necessary for the verse to include women specifically, lest you say that this statement that equates women with men in general refers only to a punishment that applies equally to an individual and to the public. But here, since it is a punishment that does not apply equally to all,

notes.he: ומשני ה"ג הני מילי לאו שיש בו מעשה - בהני עונשין שוין זה לזה דכתיב אשר יעשו דמשמע עונשין שיש בהן מעשה כגון חילול שבת ושאר איסורים שיש בהן מעשה אבל לאו שאין בו מעשה כגון תמורה דבדיבורא תליא מילתא אימא לא תילקי קמ"ל:
notes.en: And it answers; this is the reading: “These matters apply to a prohibition that involves an action”: in these punishments they are equal to one another, since it is written “shall commit [ya’asu],” which implies punishments involving an action, such as desecrating Shabbat and other prohibitions that involve an action. But for a prohibition that involves no action, such as substitution, which depends on speech alone, I might say she is not flogged. It teaches us [otherwise]. [Rashi’s reading differs from the printed text and the Davidson English, which follow the version he gives next.]

notes.dh: ל"א כתוב בספרים הני מילי עונש דשוה בין ביחיד בין בצבור
notes.he: בהאי עונש הוא דהושוו זה לזה אבל הכא בתמורה אין צבור עושין תמורה כדאמרינן באידך פירקין (דף יג.) וקא מפיק ליה ממעשר:
notes.en: Another version, written in the books: “These matters apply to a punishment that is equal for an individual and for the public”: in such a punishment they were made equal to one another. But here, with substitution, the public does not effect substitution, as we say in the other chapter (13a), and it derives this from the tithe.

notes.he: הני מילי דהשוה הכתוב אשה לאיש בעונש (דלא) דשוה בכל בין ביחיד בין בצבור אבל הכא כיון דלאו שאינו שוה בכל הוא דתנן אין הצבור כו'. ל"א ס"ד הני מילי דהשוה אשה לאיש בלאו שיש בו מעשה אבל מימר דלאו מעשה הוא אלא דיבור אימא לא תילקי קמ"ל:
notes.en: These matters, that the verse equated a woman with a man, are with a punishment that is equal for all, both for an individual and for the public; but here, since it is a prohibition that is not equal for all, as we learned: The public do not, etc. Another version: one might have thought these matters, that it equated a woman with a man, are with a prohibition that involves an action; but one who substitutes does no action, only speech, so I might say she is not flogged. It teaches us [otherwise].

messages.text: The public and partners do not render an animal a substitute,
one could claim that a woman as well, when she performs an act of substitution, is not flogged. The verse therefore teaches us that she is in fact liable.

Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom both record another reading of this answer: the verse equating a woman with a man covers only prohibitions that involve an action, while substitution is done by speech alone. Rashi gives that reading first and calls the one above the books’ version.
With regard to a minor, what is the halakha? Is he able to effect substitution or not?

What are the circumstances where this question arises? If we say that it is referring to a minor who has yet to reach the age of responsibility for his vows, i.e., twelve years and one day, you should not raise the dilemma, as since he cannot consecrate an animal by means of a vow, can he effect substitution?
messages.quote: a minor, what is the halakha

notes.he: כגון דהוי פחות מי"ב שנה דהכי אמרינן במסכת נזיר (דף סב.) איש כי יפליא מה ת"ל דהכי מצי למכתב איש כי ידור נדר אלא לרבות מופלא הסמוך לאיש כגון בן י"ב שנה דכיון שיודע להפלות לשם מי נדר ולשם מי הקדיש נדרו נדר והקדשו הקדש פחות מכן אפי' ידע למי נדר ולמי הקדיש אין בדבריו כלום יותר על כן כגון בן י"ג שנה אע"פ שאינו יודע לשם מי הפליא הוו מעשיו מעשה:
notes.en: Who has not reached the age of vows: for example, less than twelve years old. For so we say in Tractate Nazir (62a): “A man, when he shall clearly utter [yafli]”: what does the verse teach? For it could have written “A man, when he shall vow a vow.” Rather, it comes to include a discriminating minor [mufla] near manhood, for example twelve years old: since he knows how to discern in whose name he vowed and in whose name he consecrated, his vow is a vow and his consecration is consecration. Younger than that, even if he knew to whom he vowed and to whom he consecrated, his words are nothing. Older than that, for example thirteen years old, even if he does not know in whose name he uttered it, his acts are acts.

notes.he: כדפרישית לעיל דאין בדבריו כלום:
notes.en: He cannot consecrate: as I explained above, that his words are nothing.

notes.he: בתמיה כי היכי דלילקי:
notes.en: Can he effect substitution: [said] in astonishment: so that he would be flogged?

notes.he: לי"ב שנים דנדריו נבדקין:
notes.en: Who has not reached the age of vows: [that is,] twelve years, when his vows are examined.

messages.text: Rather, when he raises this dilemma, it is with regard to a minor who has reached the age of responsibility for his vows.

notes.he: דהוי בן י"ב שנה דקאמרינן התם דנדריו נבדקין ואם יודע לשם מי הפליא הוו מעשיו מעשה ואי לא לא:
notes.en: Who has reached the age of vows: that he is twelve years old, of whom we say there [in Nazir] that his vows are examined: if he knows in whose name he uttered it, his acts are acts, and if not, not.

messages.text: Do we say that a minor can effect substitution, since the Master said with regard to consecration: The verse states: “When a man shall clearly utter a vow” (Leviticus 27:2). What is the meaning when the verse states the unusual formulation: Shall clearly utter [yafli] a vow, instead of the more conventional term: Shall take a vow [yiddor]? This serves to include a discriminating minor [mufla] on the brink of adulthood, teaching that his consecration takes effect.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When anyone explicitly vows to GOD the equivalent for a human being,

notes.dh: מופלא שיודע לשם מי נודר דמצי למימר איש כי ידור נדר בערכך מה ת"ל כי יפליא כו']
notes.he: מדאקדושי מקדיש מופלא הסמוך לאיש דנודר היינו מקדיש:
notes.en: A discriminating minor: who knows in whose name he vows; for it could have said, “A man, when he shall vow a vow by your valuation”; what does the verse teach with “when he shall clearly utter”? etc. From the fact that he consecrates: a discriminating minor near manhood, who vows, that is, consecrates.

messages.text: Perhaps, from the fact that he can consecrate an animal, he can also effect substitution. Or perhaps, since no minor is subject to punishments, he cannot apply sanctity to an animal by an act of substitution, which would incur a punishment.

notes.he: עד י"ג שנה:
notes.en: He is not subject to punishments: until thirteen years.

notes.he: בה תמורה דכתיב לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו והיה הוא ותמורתו כלומר מאן דאיתיה בכלל לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר כגון בר עונשין איתיה נמי בכלל והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש דמתפיס בתמורה לאפוקי קטן דלאו בר עונשין הוא:
notes.en: It is not applied: substitution does not take hold through him, since it is written: “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it … then both it and its substitute [shall be holy].” That is, whoever is included in “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it,” such as one subject to punishments, is also included in “then both it and its substitute shall be holy,” so that he applies [sanctity] by substitution. This excludes a minor, who is not subject to punishments.

messages.text: And even if you say that a minor can perform substitution, as he will come to an age when he is subject to punishments, what is the halakha as to whether a gentile can effect substitution?

notes.dh: ואפילו אם תמצא לומר קטן עביד תמורה כו'
notes.he: רבותא אתא לאשמועינן ולא משום דאיתיה הכי:
notes.en: And even if you say that a minor can effect substitution, etc.: it comes to teach us a further novelty [about a gentile], and not because that is so [of the minor].

messages.text: Do you say that he can do so from the fact that his consecration takes effect, as it is taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “Any man [ish ish]…that brings his offering.” What is the meaning when the verse states repetitively “ish ish”? This serves to include gentiles, teaching that they can take vows to bring vow offerings and gift offerings as a Jew can.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל־בָּנָיו וְאֶל כׇּל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אִישׁ מִבֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמִן־הַגֵּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּנוֹ לְכׇל־נִדְרֵיהֶם וּלְכׇל־נִדְבוֹתָם אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה לְעֹלָה׃
verse.en:
Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the Israelite people, and say to them:
When anyone of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, presents a burnt offering as their offering for any of the votive or any of the freewill offerings that are offered to GOD,

notes.he: דהא מרבינן במנחות (דף עג:) איש איש מבני ישראל אשר יקריב קרבנו ואמרינן מה ת"ל איש איש לרבות עובדי כוכבים שנודרין נדרים ונדבות כישראל:
notes.en: From the fact that he can consecrate: for we include [this] in Menaḥot (73b): “Any man [ish ish] of the children of Israel … who brings his offering”: and we say: What does the verse teach with “ish ish”? To include gentiles, who vow vow offerings and gift offerings like a Jew.

notes.he: אשר יקריב קרבנו לכל נדריהם לרבות עובדי כוכבים:
notes.en: As it is taught: “Any man [ish ish] … who brings his offering, for any of their vows”: to include gentiles.

messages.text: Since the consecration of a gentile takes effect, perhaps he can effect substitution as well. Or perhaps, since he will not come to a time when he is subject to punishments, therefore when he performs an act of substitution, the animal is not consecrated.

notes.he: דעובד כוכבים לא לקי לעולם אבל קטן אתי לכלל עונשין כשהוא בן י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
notes.en: He will not come to be subject to punishments: for a gentile is never flogged, but a minor comes to be subject to punishments when he is thirteen years and one day old.

messages.text: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: he can effect substitution as well

messages.text: With regard to animals consecrated by gentiles, one may not derive benefit from them ab initio, but if one derived benefit from them, he is not liable for misuse of consecrated property after the fact.

notes.he: שאם נהנה מהן לא מייתי קרבן מעילה דלא דיינינן ליה כשאר קדשים שהנהנה מהן מעל משום דלא אסור בהנאה אלא מדרבנן כדלקמן:
notes.en: One may not derive benefit, and they are not subject to misuse: if one derived benefit from them he does not bring an offering for misuse, since we do not judge it like other consecrated property, where one who benefits from it has misused it; for it is forbidden for benefit only by rabbinic law, as below.

notes.he: זבחים שהעובדי כוכבים מקדישין לא נהנין ולא מועלין מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: Consecrated animals of gentiles: sacrifices that gentiles consecrate. One may not benefit from them, and they are not subject to misuse; it explains this below.

messages.text: And if one consumes them one is not liable for committing a transgression with regard to the prohibitions of piggul if they were sacrificed with the intent to consume them beyond their designated time, of notar if he consumed them beyond their designated time, and of consuming ritually impure offerings if he was impure.

notes.he: כדמסיק לקמן:
notes.en: And one is not liable for them, etc.: as it concludes below.

messages.text: Gentiles cannot render a non-sacred animal a substitute for one they consecrate.
And one does not bring libations for the offerings of a gentile as independent offerings, but his offering requires libations. This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

notes.dh: ואין מביאין כו' ה"ג ואין מביאין נסכים ול"ג עליהן
notes.he: והכי פירושא דאין מביאין נסכים של עובדי כוכבים בפני עצמן כישראל שמתנדב נסכין בפני עצמן אבל בהדי קרבנו מביאין כדאמרינן במסכת שקלים (פ"ז מ"ו) שזו אחת מן התקנות שתיקנו ב"ד דעובד כוכבים ששילח עולתו ודמי נסכיהן ממדינת הים מקבלין הימנו אבל קרבנו ודאי טעון נסכים דבהדי קרבנו מביא נסכים:
notes.en: And one does not bring, etc.: this is the reading: “And one does not bring libations,” and we do not read “for them.” And this is its explanation: one does not bring libations of gentiles by themselves, as a Jew donates libations by themselves; but together with his offering one brings them. As we say in Tractate Shekalim (7:6), this is one of the enactments the court enacted: a gentile who sent his burnt offering and the money for its libations from overseas, one accepts it from him. But his offering certainly requires libations, for together with his offering one brings libations. [The Aramaic printed on the daf does read “for them”; the Davidson English follows Rashi’s explanation.]

notes.he: פרש"י ואין מביאין של עובד כוכבים בפני עצמן כישראל שמתנדבין נסכים בפני עצמן אבל בהדי קרבנו מביאין כדאמר במסכת שקלים (דף יא עמוד ד) דזה אחת מן התקנות שהתקינו ב"ד דעובד כוכבים שמשלח עולתו ודמי נסכו ממדינת הים שמקבלין ממנו אבל ודאי קרבנו טעון נסכים דבהדי קרבנו (טעון נסכים ו) מביאין נסכים משל צבור:
notes.en: And one does not bring libations: Rashi explained: one does not bring [libations] of a gentile by themselves, as Jews donate libations by themselves, but together with his offering one brings them. As it says in Tractate Shekalim (folio 11, column 4) that this is one of the enactments the court enacted: a gentile who sends his burnt offering and the money for its libations from overseas, one accepts it from him. But his offering certainly requires libations, for together with his offering one brings libations from public funds.

notes.he: משמע הכא להאי לישנא שהעובדי כוכבים אין מביאין על קרבנן נסכים משלהן (והא דאמרינן) והא דתנן במס' שקלים עובד כוכבים ששילח עולתו ממדינת הים ושילח עמה נסכיה קריבין משלו היינו תקנת' דרבנן דז' דברים התקינו ב"ד וזה אחד מהם ולא מדאורייתא ולהאי לישנא דכתב ואין מביאין נסכים בפני עצמן היינו דאין מתנדבין להביא נסכין (בפני עצמן) בלא זבח אבל קרבנם טעון נסכים (בין) או משלהן (בין) או משל צבור דנפיק מלכל נדריהם כדמפרש בפרק ואלו מנחות:
notes.en: And one does not bring libations for them: [A printed note refers to Tosafot on Menaḥot 73b, which cites Rabbeinu Gershom’s reading here, “for them.”] According to this version it implies here that gentiles do not bring libations from their own for their offerings. And what we learned in Tractate Shekalim, that a gentile who sent his burnt offering from overseas and sent its libations with it, they are offered from his, is a rabbinic enactment, for the court enacted seven things and this is one of them; it is not Torah law. And according to the version that reads “one does not bring libations by themselves,” it means that they may not donate libations without a sacrifice, but their offering requires libations, either from their own or from public funds, as derived from “for any of their vows,” as is explained in the chapter Ve’elu Menaḥot. [A printed note adds that Menaḥot there implies that libations brought with the sacrifice need no verse, since they are part of the burnt offering and its accompaniments, and that the matter requires study.]

messages.text: With regard to all of them I see fit to be stringent.

notes.he: דלא נהנין ומועלין וחייבין עליהן משום פגול נותר וטמא כשאר קדשים חוץ מן הנסכים דודאי אין מביאין:
notes.en: With regard to all of them I see fit to be stringent: that one may not benefit from them, and they are subject to misuse, and one is liable for them on account of piggul, notar and impurity, like other consecrated property; except for the libations, which certainly one does not bring.

messages.text: In what case is this statement, that Rabbi Shimon exempts animals consecrated by gentiles from liability for misuse, said? It is said with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, i.e., offerings; but with regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, one who derives benefit from them is liable for misuse of consecrated property.

notes.he: לעיל קמהדר ואמילתיה דת"ק וה"ק בד"א דקאמר תנא קמא אינו מועלין בקדשי מזבח של עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: In what case is this said: it goes back to the first tanna’s statement, and this is what it says: Where is the first tanna’s ruling, that one is not liable for misuse, said? With a gentile’s offerings for the altar.

notes.he: שהקדישו עובד כוכבים מועלין ובמסכת זבחים מפרש טעמא בפ' ב"ש (זבחים דף מה.) ואית דגרסי לה נמי לקמן הכא בתמורה:
notes.en: But with property consecrated for Temple maintenance: which a gentile consecrated, one is liable for misuse. Tractate Zevaḥim explains the reason, in the chapter Beit Shammai (Zevaḥim 45a); and some have this reading here in Temurah as well, below.

notes.dh: במה דברים אמורים בקדשי מזבח אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מועלין
notes.he: פרש"י דאתאן לר"ש ור"י פירש דמסקנא דמילתא דר' יוסי וה"ק רבי יוסי אומר בכולן אני רואה להחמיר והא דקאמר ר"ש אין מועלין בהן בד"א בקדשי מזבח כו' ובתוספתא משמע כפרש"י דאיתא בהדיא אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מודה רבי שמעון:
notes.en: In what case is this said? With altar offerings; but with property consecrated for Temple maintenance one is liable for misuse: Rashi explained that we have come [back] to Rabbi Shimon. And the Ri explained that it is the conclusion of Rabbi Yosei’s statement, and this is what it says: Rabbi Yosei says: In all of them I see fit to be stringent; and as for what Rabbi Shimon said, that one is not liable for misuse with them, in what case is this said? With altar offerings, etc. And the Tosefta implies as Rashi explained, for it states there explicitly: But with property consecrated for Temple maintenance, Rabbi Shimon concedes.

messages.text: Rashi reads this last clause as going back to the first tanna’s words; Tosafot cite the Ri, who reads it as the end of Rabbi Yosei’s statement, and note that the Tosefta supports Rashi.
In any event, the baraita teaches that gentiles cannot render an animal a substitute for his offering.
messages.quote: cannot render a non-sacred animal a substitute

notes.he: דקדשי עובדי כוכבים אינן עושין תמורה ותיפשוט מהא:
notes.en: In any event it teaches: that the consecrated animals of gentiles do not effect substitution; so resolve [the dilemma] from this.

notes.he: וא"ת ודילמא לרבי יוסי קבעי דאמר בכולן להחמיר וי"ל דניחא ליה לאוקומי הבעיא אף לר"ש עי"ל דע"כ דלרבי יוסי לא אפשר לאוקומי הבעיא דכיון דאית ליה דעושין תמורה דאפילו את"ל דהיינו על ידי ישראל ומבעיא ליה לרמי בר חמא אם העובד כוכבים עצמו אפשר לעשותה הא לא מצית אמרת דע"כ אם ישראל מתפיסה צריך שיאמר העובד כוכבים כל הרוצה להמיר יבא וימיר ואם העובד כוכבים עצמו אין עושה תמורה היאך אפשר לעשות עולה:
notes.en: In any event it teaches: they do not effect substitution: And if you say: perhaps [Rami bar Ḥama] raises the dilemma according to Rabbi Yosei, who said he is stringent in all of them? One can say that he prefers to frame the dilemma so that it holds according to Rabbi Shimon too. Or one can further say that the dilemma necessarily cannot be framed according to Rabbi Yosei: since he holds that they do effect substitution, then even if you say that this is through a Jew, and Rami bar Ḥama asks whether the gentile himself can do it, you cannot say this. For necessarily, if a Jew applies the sanctity, the gentile must have said: Whoever wishes to substitute, let him come and substitute; and if the gentile himself does not effect substitution, how could it be done at all [literally: how could one make a burnt offering]?

messages.text: I do not raise a dilemma in a case where a gentile consecrated an animal as an offering for a gentile such as himself to achieve atonement. In this case the baraita rules explicitly that he cannot effect substitution.

notes.he: כלומר אי משום הא לא איריא דמהכא ליכא למיפשט כלל דהיכא דהקדיש עובד כוכבים להתכפר עובד כוכבים שהפרישו לצורך כפרת עצמו:
notes.en: He said to him: in the case of the consecration of gentiles: that is, if it is because of this, there is no proof, for from here nothing at all can be resolved: [it speaks] where a gentile consecrated for a gentile to achieve atonement, that he set it aside for his own atonement. [Rashi’s text reads “He said to him” here.]

notes.he: דאין הקדשו עושה תמורה הואיל ולא אתי לכלל עונשין:
notes.en: I do not raise a dilemma: that his consecrated animal does not effect substitution, since he will not come to be subject to punishments.

messages.text: When I raise the dilemma, it is in a case where a gentile consecrated an animal as an offering and a Jew achieves atonement with it. In this situation, do we follow the one who consecrated it, in which case the gentile cannot effect substitution, or do we follow the one achieving atonement, in which case he can?

notes.he: שהפרישו עובד כוכבים לצורך ישראל שיתכפר בו ישראל:
notes.en: And a Jew achieves atonement: that a gentile set it aside for a Jew, so that the Jew would achieve atonement with it.

notes.he: והמקדיש הוי עובד כוכבים דלא אתי לכלל עונשין ואינו עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Do we follow the one who consecrated: and the one who consecrated is a gentile, who will not come to be subject to punishments, and so does not effect substitution.

notes.he: שהוא ישראל ואיתיה בכלל מלקות:
notes.en: Or the one achieving atonement: who is a Jew, and is subject to flogging.

notes.he: דמועלין בהן וחייבין משום פגול כו'] אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מועלין. דקדשי ה' נינהו [ולרמי בר חמא דקא בעי לה קסבר מהכא לא תפשוט דהקדיש עובד כוכבים להתכפר עובד כוכבים לא קא מיבעיא ליה. דודאי אין עושין תמורה כי קא מבעיא ליה הקדיש עובד כוכבים להתכפר ישראל לפטור חובתו של ישראל בתר מקדיש אזלינן ומקדיש עובד כוכבים הוא ואין עושה תמורה או בתר מתכפר דישראל הוא אזלינן ועושה תמורה:
notes.en: In all of them to be stringent: that they are subject to misuse, and one is liable for piggul, etc. But with property consecrated for Temple maintenance they are subject to misuse, since it is the Lord’s holy property. And Rami bar Ḥama, who raises the dilemma, holds that one cannot resolve it from here: where a gentile consecrated for a gentile to achieve atonement he does not raise the dilemma, for certainly they do not effect substitution. When he raises the dilemma, it is where a gentile consecrated for a Jew to achieve atonement, to discharge the Jew’s obligation: do we follow the one who consecrated, and the one who consecrated is a gentile, who does not effect substitution; or do we follow the one achieving atonement, who is a Jew, and he effects substitution?

messages.text: Solve this dilemma by invoking a statement of Rabbi Abbahu,
messages.quote: or do we follow the one achieving atonement

notes.dh: ה"ג תיפשוט ליה מהא דאמר ר' אבהו
notes.he: לקמן:
notes.en: This is the reading: “Resolve it from what Rabbi Abbahu said”: below.

messages.text: If one consecrates an animal as an offering to be brought by another, and the animal develops a blemish disqualifying it for sacrifice, if the one who consecrated it desires to redeem it, he adds one-fifth to its value, just as he would were it his own offering. By contrast, if the one achieving atonement with the offering desires to redeem it, he does not need to add one-fifth.
messages.lead: as Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

notes.he:
שאם רוצה לפדות הקדשו כגון שנפל בו מום יכול לפדותו ומוסיף חומש אבל מימר אינו מוסיף חומש דכתיב אם המקדיש וגו' (ויקרא כז) על הקדש ראשון אתה מוסיף חומש ולא על הקדש שני כגון תמורה:
ע"א שאם הקדיש בית או שדה ואתו בעלים לפדותו לא פרקי בלא חומש דכתיב (שם) ואם המקדיש יגאל ויסף חמישיתו אבל אם גאלו אחר לא חייביה רחמנא ליתן חומש:
notes.en: One who consecrates adds one-fifth: if he wishes to redeem his consecrated animal, for example because a blemish developed in it, he can redeem it, and he adds one-fifth; but one who substitutes does not add one-fifth, as it is written: “And if he that consecrated it [will redeem it]” (Leviticus 27): for the first consecration you add one-fifth, and not for a second consecration such as a substitute. Another explanation: if he consecrated a house or a field and the owners came to redeem it, they do not redeem it without a fifth, as it is written (ibid.): “And if he that consecrated it will redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part”; but if another redeemed it, the Merciful One did not obligate him to give a fifth.

notes.he: מקדיש מוסיף חומש כשהוא גואל הקדשו:
notes.en: One who consecrates adds one-fifth when he redeems his consecrated property.

messages.text: But the one achieving atonement with the offering can render another animal a substitute for it as if he had consecrated it.

notes.he: שאם הפריש ישראל קרבן כדי שיתכפר בו חבירו ישראל ואמר המתכפר זו תחת זו תמורתו תמורה ולוקה דכיון שהופרש לצורכו קרינא ביה קרבנו דבתר המתכפר אזלינן ותיפשוט מהא:
notes.en: And the one achieving atonement effects substitution: if a Jew set aside an offering so that his fellow Jew would achieve atonement with it, and the one achieving atonement said, “This is in place of this,” his substitute is a substitute and he is flogged. Since it was set aside for his sake, we call it “his offering,” for we follow the one achieving atonement. So resolve [the dilemma] from this.

notes.he: אלמא בתר מתכפר אזלינן:
notes.en: And the one achieving atonement effects substitution: evidently we follow the one achieving atonement.

messages.text: And if one separates teruma, the portion of produce designated for a priest, from his own produce…

notes.he: מתבואה שלו על טבלין של חבירו לפוטרו מן המעשרות:
notes.en: And one who separates teruma: from his own grain for another’s untithed produce, to exempt it from the tithes.

messages.text: Continued on 3a: “…for the produce of another, the benefit of discretion is his.” Rami bar Ḥama could answer that there the offering was a Jew’s from start to finish; his dilemma is whether the animal must be in the hands of one who can effect substitution from its consecration to its sacrifice, and it stands unresolved (teiku).
